takeaway: High anion gap metabolic acidosis: unmeasured anions accumulate, as in ketoacidosis and lactic acidosis. A normal gap acidosis can also occur.

question.text: Which condition is associated with a metabolic acidosis and a high anion gap?

lines.text: Here is the anion gap, balanced on a seesaw.
The gap is the measured sodium and potassium, minus bicarbonate and chloride.
When it is high, unmeasured anions are piling up: ketones, lactate, organic acids.
Ketoacidosis is the classic cause, with its fruity breath of acetone. That is our answer.
(sigh) Lactic acidosis, the tired little sugar cube, behaves the same way.
But careful: a metabolic acidosis can also have a normal gap, so the gap tells them apart.
